newsitem.title: LEBANON: South Lebanon rockets wound two Israeli soldiers.
newsitem.headline: South Lebanon rockets wound two Israeli soldiers.

text.p: Two Israeli soldiers were wounded on Friday when Hizbollah guerrillas fired Katyusha rockets into outposts inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, pro-Israeli militia and Hizbollah sources said.
South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia sources said guerrillas fired three salvoes of rockets into the Israeli outposts of Marqaba and Blat on the Lebanese side of the border early in the morning.
Two Israeli soldiers were wounded in the attacks, they added.
In Jerusalem, an Israeli army spokesman said one Israeli soldier was wounded by mortar fire.
"One Israeli soldier was wounded in moderate condition during the early morning hours by mortar shells which were fired at an Israeli army position on the Lebanon border," the spokesman said.
He said guerrillas were simultaneously firing shells at Isareli and SLA positions in the eastern and western sectors of the zone.
"Israeli forces returned fire in the direction of the source of the fire," the spokesman added.
There were no immediate reports of casualties in the retaliatory Israeli shelling.
In Beirut, pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) said its guerrillas fired three salvoes of Katyusha rockets into the border outposts.
Until Friday, six Israeli soldiers had been killed and 26 wounded in guerrilla attacks in south Lebanon since the beginning of the year.
Hizbollah guerrillas attack the Israeli soldiers and their SLA allies in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine-mile) wide occupation zone.
